summary: The SQLite bindings are unusually well-tested: the vtable, UDF/UDAF/window, and query_to_array surfaces all have deep coverage of error/leak/NaN/NUL/cross-process-cache/pushdown-edge paths, and the value/result accessors are round-tripped with documented skips. The genuine gaps are concentrated in the table-valued-function (register_tvf) surface, whose string/unicode/blob OUTPUT-column codepath (a whole branch of _tvf_xcolumn plus the per-cursor scratch path) is never exercised, and in a few minor edge/doc items (typemap module missing from sphinx docs, oversized-cell truncation in query_to_array, truncated-multibyte UTF-8, and thin _sqlite_constants value assertions).

findings.title: register_tvf string/unicode/blob output columns are never tested
findings.claim: Every register_tvf test uses an int/float-only out_dtype (test_sqlite_tvf.py: _OUT=dtype([('n','i8')]), _OUT2=dtype([('n','i8'),('v','f8')]); the vtable tests reuse the same int64 series tvf). The _tvf_xcolumn factory's _TAG_S (text), _TAG_U (unicode, decoded via utf32_to_utf8 into the per-cursor scratch with SQLITE_TRANSIENT) and _TAG_BLOB branches are therefore never executed, and the per-cursor scratch allocation (_tvf_xopen scratch_p / _build_tvf_descriptor scratch_bytes) is never sized non-zero. A wrong offset, width//4, scratch-size, or TRANSIENT/STATIC choice in the tvf string path would ship undetected even though the analogous register_table path is exhaustively tested. A TVF returning a 'U'/'S' structured column is a realistic use (the docstring and _SQL_TYPE map advertise it).
findings.evidence: _tvf_xcolumn (lines 330-343) has: `elif tag == _TAG_S: n = _nul_trimmed_len(addr, widths[j]); sqlite3_result_text(ctx, addr, int32(n), _SQLITE_TRANSIENT)` ... `elif tag == _TAG_U: scratch = c[0].scratch_p; n = utf32_to_utf8(addr, widths[j] // 4, scratch); sqlite3_result_text(ctx, scratch, int32(n), _SQLITE_TRANSIENT)` ... `elif tag == _TAG_BLOB: ...`. `_build_tvf_descriptor` (line 394) computes `scratch = max([w + 1 for w, t in zip(vis_widths, vis_tags) if t == _TAG_U], default=0)`. grep of test/core/test_sqlite_tvf.py and test_sqlite_vtable.py shows register_tvf is only ever called with arg/out dtypes np.int64/np.float64 (_OUT, _OUT2); no 'U4'/'S4'/text/blob out column.
findings.recommendation: Add a register_tvf test whose out_dtype includes a 'U' (e.g. U6), an 'S' (e.g. S4), and a BLOB column, asserting round-trip through sqlite3_column_text/_blob/_bytes (mirror test_structured_text_and_unicode / test_two_unicode_columns_single_cursor from test_sqlite_vtable.py, including an interior-NUL and a multi-byte/emoji codepoint to exercise scratch sizing and the TRANSIENT path).

findings.title: _sqlite_typemap module absent from sphinx docs (no automodule, not in conventions list)
findings.lines: 22-26 (conventions family list); Modules section (507-625, no _sqlite_typemap entry)
findings.claim: _sqlite_typemap.py is a module under numbox/core/bindings/ with a module-level docstring and documented helper functions (utf32_to_utf8, utf8_to_utf32, _nul_trimmed_len, _col_tag) that the vtable, tvf, and query_to_array all depend on, but it has no `.. automodule:: numbox.core.bindings._sqlite_typemap` section and is not named in the 'Bindings module conventions' family list. CLAUDE.md's docs rule says a new _*.py bindings module gets an automodule section added. Sphinx will silently omit this module's docstring and its UTF-8/UTF-32 transcoding contract from the rendered API docs; the family list is also stale.
findings.evidence: grep 'typemap' over docs/numbox.core.bindings.rst returns no match. The Modules section (lines 507-625) has automodule directives for _sqlite_conn through _sqlite_tvf but none for _sqlite_typemap. The conventions list (lines 22-26) enumerates _sqlite_conn/_stmt/_bind/_column/_exec/_blob/_hooks/_constants/_sqlite_value/_sqlite_result/_sqlite_udf/_sqlite_query/_sqlite_tvf but not _sqlite_typemap (nor _sqlite_udf_helpers / _sqlite_vtable, though those two at least have automodule sections at lines 595/603).
findings.recommendation: Add a `numbox.core.bindings._sqlite_typemap` automodule section (members/undoc-members/show-inheritance, matching the siblings) and add _sqlite_typemap to the conventions family list; while there, add the also-omitted _sqlite_udf_helpers and _sqlite_vtable to that family list for consistency.

findings.title: query_to_array oversized-cell truncation (nbytes >= field width) for TEXT/BLOB/U is untested
findings.lines: 111-126 (_store_cell _TAG_U/_TAG_S/_TAG_BLOB); 117, 124 (nn = nbytes if nbytes < width else width)
findings.claim: _store_cell silently truncates a result cell whose byte length exceeds the destination field width (S/BLOB via `nn = nbytes if nbytes < width else width`; U via _put_unicode clamping to `width // 4`). Every query_to_array text/blob test uses cells that fit (test_query_text_roundtrip 'héllo' into U8; test_query_blob_into_S_field x'00ff10' into S3; test_query_empty_text_and_blob empties). No test feeds a TEXT/BLOB/U value LONGER than the dtype field, so the truncation boundary (and that it does not overrun buf) is unverified -- a realistic data-loss path on a too-narrow dtype.
findings.evidence: Lines 116-119: `src = carray(_cast_int_to_void_p(src_p), (nbytes,), dtype=np.uint8); nn = nbytes if nbytes < width else width; for b in range(nn): buf[off + b] = src[b]` (same shape for _TAG_BLOB at 121-126). For _TAG_U, line 112 passes `width // 4` as width_cp into _put_unicode, whose loop is `while i < nbytes and k < width_cp`. test_sqlite_query.py has no case where a returned TEXT/BLOB exceeds the dtype field width.
findings.recommendation: Add a query_to_array test selecting a TEXT longer than the 'U'/'S' field (e.g. 'abcdef' into U4 and into S4) and a BLOB longer than its 'S' field, asserting the truncated prefix and that no adjacent field is corrupted.

findings.title: utf8_to_utf32 truncated multi-byte sequence at end-of-buffer is untested
findings.claim: utf8_to_utf32's multi-byte branches require the full sequence to be present (`i + 1 < nbytes`, `i + 2 < nbytes`, `i + 3 < nbytes`); a lead byte at the very end of the buffer with missing continuation bytes falls through to the else branch (cp = 0xFFFD, i += 1). The decode tests in test_sqlite_query.py cover bad-continuation, surrogate, overlong, and clamp-to-width, but none feed a TRUNCATED sequence (e.g. a lone 0xC2 or 0xE2 0x82 as the last bytes). That boundary -- the difference between '<' and '<=' in the guards -- is unverified.
findings.evidence: Line 83: `elif b0 >> 5 == 0x6 and i + 1 < nbytes and (inp[i + 1] >> 6) == 0x2:` (2-byte); the trailing `else: cp = 0xFFFD; i += 1` (lines 100-102) is the only path for a lead byte whose continuation runs past nbytes. test_sqlite_query.py decode tests: test_utf8_to_utf32_bad_continuation_is_replacement (0xE0 0x20 0x41 -- full length), _surrogate (0xED 0xA0 0x80 -- full), _overlong (0xC0 0xAF -- full); no lone-trailing-lead-byte case.
findings.recommendation: Add a _decode case with a truncated sequence at the buffer tail (e.g. b'A\xc2' and b'A\xe2\x82') asserting the lead byte decodes to U+FFFD and the preceding char is intact; this also guards the equivalent _put_unicode loop in _sqlite_query.py.

findings.title: test_sqlite_constants asserts only the 8 index-constraint ops; result/type/flag/destructor values unguarded
findings.claim: _sqlite_constants.py defines ~60 SQLITE_* values that must match the SQLite C headers (result codes 0-101, type codes 1-5, open flags, blob flags, trace bits, and the load-bearing destructor sentinels SQLITE_STATIC=0 / SQLITE_TRANSIENT=-1, plus UDF flags). The only value-assertion test pins the 8 SQLITE_INDEX_CONSTRAINT_* ops. A typo in any other constant (e.g. SQLITE_TRANSIENT, whose -1 is the documented copy-the-buffer sentinel; or SQLITE_OPEN_* bit masks) would only be caught indirectly by whichever integration test happens to exercise it, and several (e.g. SQLITE_DIRECTONLY, SQLITE_INNOCUOUS, SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX, the trace bits other than STMT) are not exercised anywhere.
findings.evidence: test_sqlite_constants.py contains a single test, test_index_constraint_ops, asserting `(...) == (2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 68, 71, 72)`. _sqlite_constants.py lines 40-125 define result codes, type codes, open flags (0x1..0x40000), blob flags, trace bits (0x01..0x08), destructor sentinels (SQLITE_STATIC=0, SQLITE_TRANSIENT=-1), and UDF flags (SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC=0x800, SQLITE_DIRECTONLY=0x80000, SQLITE_INNOCUOUS=0x200000, SQLITE_SUBTYPE=0x100000, SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE=0x1000000) -- none value-asserted in the test file.
findings.recommendation: Extend test_sqlite_constants.py with value assertions for the result codes (esp. SQLITE_OK/ROW/DONE), the five type codes, SQLITE_STATIC/SQLITE_TRANSIENT, the open/blob/trace flags, and the UDF flag bits, cross-checked against Python's stdlib sqlite3 constants where available (e.g. sqlite3.SQLITE_OK) to catch header drift.
